notes: Account: mid-tier quant research team at large EU wealth manager; building a unified knowledge portal for analysts and PMs.
Primary problem: slow, noisy search across 30M+ documents (research notes, SEC filings, transcripts). Need sub-150ms retrieval + accurate reranking at scale.
Scale ask: ingest initially ~30M documents, target 200M vectors after augmentation (embeddings per section), must support incremental daily ingestion of ~100k docs.
Indexing architecture preference: hybrid sparse+dense, IVF/PQ style vector store with offline quantization for cost reduction; support for shard-level routing and warm KVS.

Reranking: plan to deploy a cross-encoder fine-tuned on internal relevance labels (10k labeled pairs). Want Redwood to host small cross-encoder reranker co-located with vector shards to hit latency SLOs.
Latency/throughput targets: 95th pctile end-to-end query <= 200ms, median <= 120ms; baseline QPS 150 sustained, burst 600 for research spikes.
Cost sensitivity: target amortized per-query cost < $0.004 (embedding lookup + rerank). Interested in Redwood Optimize suggestions for batching and quantization tradeoffs.
Deployment: dedicated capacity preferred (reserved GPUs). Must run in EU region and integrate with customer's KMS/HSM for key ownership.
Security: strict data residency, retention controls, immutable audit logs, SSO via SAML, SOC2 and ISO required. Customer will share a security questionnaire.
POC ask: 3-week bench POC — index 200k representative docs, run standardized RAG queries, measure latency/cost and quality (MRR/NDCG).
Quote from CTO: 'We need predictable tail latency and a clear path to <€0.004/query at scale — no vendor black boxes on keys.'
Success criteria: demonstrable indexing throughput, 95p latency within SLO on dedicated pool, reranker improves top-5 precision by 18% vs current BM25 baseline.
Integration notes: connectors for SFTP and internal DMS planned; dev team will provide anonymized sample dataset for POC.
Procurement: legal asked for KMS/HSM architecture diagram; finance requested 36-month commit pricing for Dedicated.
CS/SE ask: include fallback policy to hosted lower-cost model for non-sensitive workloads and routing by cost/latency per query type.
Misc: prefer transparent benchmarking numbers and token-level cost breakdowns; wants runbook for incident recovery and model fallback.
Sales tact: PLG -> AE engaged after inbound; technical evaluation with SE-led POC; likely Dedicated purchase if POC meets SLAs.
